text:
alex: Heads up — after yesterday's routing policy canary we started seeing a small reconnect spike plus double-counted tokens on resumes. Console shows duplicate resume hooks for same session id. Anyone else?
maya: saw the alerts, looked briefly. spike is ~0.8% of requests in eu-west. not sure if billing or quota dup yet.
devon: I repro'd locally with a tiny script — if the proxy flips route during resume we end up delivering 'resume' to both old and new backend for ~200ms. logs: `resume_id=abc123 handled_by=[route-a,route-b]`
carla: dashboard note: the resume event count panel has been spiking but the trace panel only shows one active trace id. sampler might be dropping the second resume traces.
alex: here's the minimal curl SSE repro I used: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.dev.redwood/stream?sess=abc"` then trigger route swap (scale-down) — you'll see resume frames followed by two billing events.
maya: is this strictly a routing policy change interaction, or would any sticky->stateless switch trigger it?
devon: it's sticky->sticky with lease handoff. the old proxy forwards the resume to the old runtime while the routing layer also replays to new runtime due to our fallback fanout. fanout+lease-renew race = double-delivery.
carla: ops note: Console counts come from two places: billing-emitter and session-metrics. billing-emitter deduplicates by token but only if `resume_id` present. our resume frames sometimes lose resume_id when proxied through the canary (header rewrite bug).
alex: so two problems: (1) fanout on route-swap causing duplicate attempts, (2) header/trace attr strip on canary proxy that prevents dedupe.
devon: quick fix proposal: stop fanout on route-change for resume type events (only do failover single-target), add explicit resume_id propagation assertion in proxy. fallback to fanout only on explicit capacity-failures.
maya: agree. stopping fanout at least prevents billing duplicates. can we add a console flag to rollback fanout behavior per-tenant?
alex: yes, we can gate via routing policy toggle in the console. I'll open a tiny UI flag patch.
carla: telemetry action: add `resume.attempt_index` and `resume.duplicate=true/false` tags to billing traces so we can alert when duplicates > 0. Also increase the resume trace sampling rate for next 24h.
devon: ops quick patch: PR incoming to proxy to preserve `x-resume-id` and `x-trace-id` in canary mode. also logging `resume_via` with route name.
deploy-bot: canary deploy note — the routing-policy change rolled to 10% eu-west at 03:12UTC yesterday. No automated rollback triggered.
maya: Timeline: 03:12 canary, 03:40 first spike, 04:05 alerts. Rollback pending decision.
alex: decision: roll the routing-policy flag back to previous behavior for all canaries immediately, then deploy proxy header fix behind feature flag.
carla: I'll wire a one-off dashboard that shows billing events where `resume.duplicate=true` and tag affected tenants.
devon: FYI test harness: adding this case to the streaming e2e suite — simulate midstream route-swap and assert single resume deliver.
maya: thanks — assign owners? alex (console flag rollback), devon (proxy header fix + e2e), carla (telemetry + dashboard). I'll create tasks.
alex: thanks team. rough ETA for rollback + patch: rollback 30m, proxy PR in 2hrs, telemetry roll in 4hrs. ping me if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
